corrected_value.title_o: The curse of knowledge: First language knowledge impairs adult learners’ use of novel statistics for word segmentation

decisions.quote:
We replicated Exp. 3 of Finn & Hudson Kam (2008) The curse of knowledge: First language
                    knowledge impairs adult learners’ use of novel statistics for word segmentation, Cognition,
                    108, 477-499. This experiment was part of a larger project to systematically replicate as many
                    experiments involving statistical word learning in adults as possible.
decisions.reason: The title, abstract, introduction, and reference list explicitly identify Experiment 3 of Finn & Hudson Kam (2008), 'The curse of knowledge: First language knowledge impairs adult learners’ use of novel statistics for word segmentation,' Cognition, 108(2), 477-499, as the sole original study re-tested by this replication (Experiment 1 is mentioned only as background context within the original paper).

decisions.quote: Thus, we were unable to confirm the findings of FHK08.
decisions.reason: Using FHK08's original t-test analysis on the new sample, participants discriminated trained words above chance in both non-word and split-word foil conditions with no difference between conditions, failing to confirm FHK08. Although revised binomial mixed-effects models on the replication sample showed significant learning in non-word trials and non-significant learning in split-word trials when analyzed separately, the critical difference between foil types remained statistically indistinguishable (p = .70). Under Codebook Step 3 Rule 1, the authors' explicit overall verdict ('Thus, we were unable to confirm the findings of FHK08.') governs over partially agreeing revised analyses.

We replicated Exp. 3 of Finn & Hudson Kam (2008) The curse of knowledge: First language
                    knowledge impairs adult learners’ use of novel statistics for word segmentation, Cognition,

decisions.reason: The authors collected new empirical data from 39 Amazon Mechanical Turk participants (50 recruited, 11 excluded) using FHK08's stimuli to re-test Experiment 3 of Finn & Hudson Kam (2008). Both the 'Original Analyses' and 'Revised Analyses' sections analyze this newly collected replication sample rather than re-analyzing FHK08's original dataset, establishing the record type as replication.
